correctness.rationale: Independently, normalize ∑|c_j|²=1 and put T=|F_c|². Then 0≤T≤4, E[T]=1, and E[T²]=2−∑|c_j|⁴≤7/4 by orthogonality and the twelve distinct nonzero ordered differences. The pointwise nonnegativity of (4−T)(T−3/4)² gives E[T³]≤(11/2)E[T²]−(105/16)E[T]+9/4≤85/16. Equality requires T(x)∈{3/4,4} everywhere, and the mean forces T(x)=4 somewhere. Cauchy–Schwarz at that point makes c proportional to the character vector with opposite frequency phases to x. Conversely a normalized such vector has T=4 once and T=3/4 at all other x, by the difference-set character-sum identity; its third moment attains the bound. The distinct phases are detected in the e=1 coordinate, giving exactly 13 projective lines. The sixth power, not the norm itself, is 85/16.
